healthcare.summary: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Egypt. Emergency numbers (122/123/180), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccination requirements, water safety, and travel insurance advice.

recommended: Meningococcal meningitis (for travel during Hajj season)
Polio (ensure adult booster if traveling to certain areas)
vaccinations.notes: No required vaccinations for most travelers unless arriving from a yellow fever endemic country. COVID-19 requirements vary — check current entry requirements. Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date. Consider hepatitis A and typhoid for all travelers.

pharmacy.hours: Most pharmacies open 9am-11pm; many 24-hour pharmacies in major cities; pharmacy chains include Oscar, Seif, and Nile Pharmacies
pharmacy.tips: Many medications available OTC that require prescriptions in the US. Antibiotics and common drugs are easily found. Pharmacists are helpful. Bring a list with generic names. Some medications may not be available — bring your supply. In tourist areas (Sharm el-Sheikh, Hurghada), pharmacies are well-stocked.

water.notes: Tap water is NOT safe to drink in Egypt. Use bottled or filtered water for drinking and brushing teeth. Avoid ice in drinks outside of hotels and reputable restaurants. Bottled water is very cheap and widely available. Waterborne diseases are a risk if you consume tap water.

healthcare.foodSafetyTips: Be cautious with food from street vendors. In hotels, resorts, and reputable restaurants, food is generally safe. Avoid raw salads and uncooked foods outside of upscale establishments. Egyptian cuisine (koshari, grilled meats, falafel) from busy restaurants is generally safe. Avoid dairy products from informal sources. In Red Sea resorts, restaurants maintain good hygiene standards.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Required for visa on arrival / e-visa travelers. Strongly recommended for all travelers.
travelInsurance.tips: Travel insurance is strongly recommended. Public hospitals are basic; private hospitals offer good care. Medical evacuation coverage is essential, especially for Red Sea diving injuries (which require treatment in a recompression chamber) and remote desert areas. Ensure coverage includes medical evacuation to Europe if needed.

healthcare.qualityNotes: Private hospitals in Cairo and Alexandria offer good quality care comparable to Western standards at a fraction of the cost. Public hospitals are basic and under-resourced. Many private doctors speak English and/or French. Pharmacies (pharmacies) are widely available, often open late.

medications.generalAdvice: Egypt has very strict drug laws with severe penalties including lengthy prison sentences. All medications should be carried in original packaging with a doctor's letter in English. The Egyptian Ministry of Health requires advance approval for importing certain controlled substances — contact the Egyptian embassy before travel if you take controlled medications.

controlledSubstances.note: Cannabis is completely illegal in Egypt with severe penalties including imprisonment. This includes CBD products. Egyptian drug laws are aggressively enforced — do not bring any cannabis-related products.

Tramadol is particularly strictly controlled in Egypt due to widespread abuse. Carry original prescription, doctor's letter, and a permit from the Egyptian Ministry of Health if possible. Only bring the amount needed for your stay.

Controlled substances requiring a permit from the Egyptian Ministry of Health. Bring original prescription, doctor's letter, and only the amount needed. Declare at customs. Contact the Egyptian embassy before travel.
Controlled substances. Carry documentation and doctor's letter. Declare at customs.
Controlled substances in Egypt. Carry doctor's letter and prescription documentation.
Illegal in Egypt. Possession carries severe penalties.

connectivity.simOptions: Vodafone Egypt, Orange, or Etisalat prepaid SIMs at airport arrivals hall. Need passport. Data plans very cheap — ~50 EGP for 10GB.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at most hotels and many cafes in Cairo and tourist areas. Quality can be unreliable. Limited in Upper Egypt and desert areas.
connectivity.bestOption: Vodafone Egypt prepaid SIM at Cairo airport — counters open 24/7. Best coverage nationwide. eSIM via Airalo as alternative.

cultural.tipping: Expected everywhere. 10-15% at restaurants. Tip guides, drivers, hotel staff. Baksheesh (small tips) is part of daily life — carry small bills.
cultural.dressCode: Modest dress, especially for women. Cover shoulders and knees, particularly at mosques. Women should bring a headscarf for mosque visits. Men should wear long pants at religious sites.
cultural.greetings: Handshake common between same gender. Men should wait for a woman to extend her hand first. 'As-salamu alaykum' (peace be upon you) is the standard greeting.
taboos: Using left hand to eat or pass items
Showing the soles of your feet
Photography of military installations or government buildings
Drinking alcohol in public during Ramadan
cultural.haggling: Expected and essential at bazaars, markets, and with taxi drivers. Start at 25-40% of asking price. Take your time — haggling is a social ritual.

safety.lgbtSafety: Egypt is not safe for LGBTQ+ travelers. Same-sex relations are not explicitly criminalized but authorities use 'debauchery' laws to prosecute LGBTQ+ individuals. There have been arrests and crackdowns — extreme discretion is essential. Avoid dating apps, as police have used them for entrapment.
safety.soloFemaleSafety: Solo female travel in Egypt requires significant awareness. Street harassment and catcalling are very common, especially in Cairo and tourist areas. Dress conservatively, avoid walking alone at night, and consider joining group tours for sites outside major cities.
safety.notes: Egypt is generally safe for tourists in well-traveled areas like Cairo, Luxor, Giza, and Red Sea resorts. Petty crime such as scams and aggressive touts are the main concerns. Avoid the Sinai Peninsula border areas and Western Desert regions. Terrorism risk exists but major tourist sites have heavy security.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: visa on arrival (USD $25) or e-Visa. UK, EU also eligible for visa on arrival. Single entry, 30 days.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: October-April (cooler). December-February most pleasant. Avoid June-August (extreme heat 40°C+). Ramadan dates vary — plan accordingly.

hospitals.name: As-Salam International Hospital
hospitals.notes: Best hospital for tourists in Cairo. English-speaking staff, accepts international insurance.

immediate: Drink 3-4 liters of water per day
Wear loose, light-colored clothing and sun protection
Avoid prolonged exposure when temperatures exceed 40°C
after: Seek medical care for signs of heat stroke: hot dry skin, confusion

steps: File a police report immediately — get the report number, you will need it
Contact the US Embassy or nearest consulate: Contact the nearest US Embassy
Bring the police report + any ID you have (driver's license, copy of passport)
Apply for an Emergency Passport (usually issued within 1-2 business days)
Notify your travel insurance and airline of the situation
stolenPassport.notes: Keep a digital copy of your passport in cloud storage (Google Photos, iCloud) and email yourself a scan before travel.

steps: Go to the nearest police station (or call 122)
Bring ID or a copy of your passport if available
Request a written report — ask for an English copy or certified translation if needed
Keep the report number safe — required for insurance claims
For theft: list all stolen items with approximate values
policeReport.notes: In many countries, tourist police stations are available in major cities — they have English-speaking staff. Ask your hotel concierge for the nearest tourist police.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured
Call police (122) and ambulance (123) if there are injuries
Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties
Document the scene with photos before moving vehicles
Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the RIGHT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is recommended for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.
